result.question: How does Nvidia characterize the impact of export controls on its business with China?
result.answer:
Nvidia characterizes the impact of export controls on its business with China as already harmful and potentially far-reaching. Nvidia states that its competitive position has already been harmed by existing export controls, and that its competitive position and future results may be further harmed over the long term if there are further changes in the USG's export controls [0001045810-25-000023:item-1-p016]. In the event of such changes, Nvidia warns it may be unable to sell its inventory of affected products and may be unable to develop replacement products not subject to the licensing requirements, effectively excluding it from all or part of the China market, as well as other impacted markets including the Middle East and countries designated "Tier 2" by the AI Diffusion IFR [0001045810-25-000023:item-1-p016].

Nvidia states that export controls have had and are likely in the future to have a disproportionate impact on NVIDIA and may disadvantage it against certain competitors that sell chips outside the scope of such controls [0001045810-25-000230:part-ii--item-1a-p017]. Export controls have already encouraged and may in the future encourage customers outside China and other impacted regions to "design-out" certain U.S. semiconductors from their products to reduce the compliance burden and risk [0001045810-25-000230:part-ii--item-1a-p017]. Export controls have also encouraged and may in the future encourage overseas governments to request that Nvidia's customers purchase from its competitors rather than NVIDIA or other U.S. firms, harming its business, market position, and financial results [0001045810-25-000230:part-ii--item-1a-p017].

Nvidia states that export controls may negatively impact demand for its products and services not only in China, but also in other markets such as Europe, Latin America, and Southeast Asia [0001045810-25-000230:part-ii--item-1a-p017]. Nvidia states that export controls increase the risk of investing in U.S. advanced semiconductor products, because by the time a new product is ready for market, it may be subject to new unilateral export controls restricting its sale, resulting in excess inventory and purchase obligations as it recently experienced with the H20 [0001045810-25-000230:part-ii--item-1a-p017]. At the same time, such controls may increase investment in foreign competitors, which would be less likely to be restricted by U.S. controls [0001045810-25-000230:part-ii--item-1a-p017].

Nvidia also warns that any regulatory control that limits its ability to provide products and services supporting third-party applications and models, including applications built on foundation models originating in China such as DeepSeek, Qwen, or KIMMI, could have a material impact on its business, operating results, and financial condition [0001045810-25-000230:part-ii--item-1a-p017]. Export controls may also disrupt Nvidia's supply and distribution chain for a substantial portion of its products, which are warehoused in and distributed from Hong Kong [0001045810-25-000230:part-ii--item-1a-p017]. Export controls restricting Nvidia's ability to sell data center GPUs may also negatively impact demand for its networking products used in servers containing its GPUs [0001045810-25-000230:part-ii--item-1a-p017].

Nvidia states that new and existing export controls or changes to existing export controls could limit alternative manufacturing locations and negatively impact its business, given its supply chain is currently concentrated in the Asia-Pacific region [0001045810-25-000023:item-1-p017]. Nvidia states that the United States has imposed unilateral worldwide controls restricting GPUs and associated products, and it is likely that additional unilateral or multilateral controls will be adopted [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a-p031]. Such controls have been and may again be very broad in scope and application, could prohibit Nvidia from exporting its products to any or all customers in one or more markets, and could negatively impact its manufacturing, testing, and warehousing locations and options, or could impose other conditions that limit its ability to serve demand abroad and could negatively and materially impact its business, revenue, and financial results [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a-p031]. Controls could also negatively impact Nvidia's cost and/or ability to provide services such as NVIDIA AI cloud services and could impact the cost and/or ability for its CSPs and customers to provide services to their end customers, even outside China [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a-p031]. The possibility of additional export controls has negatively impacted and may in the future negatively impact demand for Nvidia's products, benefiting competitors that offer alternatives less likely to be restricted by further controls [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a-p031]. Repeated changes in the export control rules are likely to impose compliance burdens on Nvidia's business and its customers, negatively and materially impacting its business [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a-p031].
